claim: Qualified native memory maintenance using nine pinned repository sources, upstream commands and unchanged tests; enabled hourly learning and bounded assistant outcome capture, preserving scope and privacy choices. Independent state inspection and native Claude source review distinguish admission, model review and actual capture.
limitations: Current-host memory maintenance and bounded client capture, not universal SOTA superiority or every memory repository installed.

Two accelerated scheduler ticks were observed; both preflight-skipped without LLM calls. Final hourly configuration persisted across service restart, but no later hourly tick or physical-PC reboot is claimed.
Manual learning rejected insufficient durable evidence and applied no proposal. New learned-write quality and future retrieval improvement remain unmeasured.
All database scopes enter the scheduler, one review per project per tick; current scope count is one. Claims are once per session including preflight-skipped sessions.
Claude prompt capture remains opted out. Assistant excerpts are sanitized and capped at 2000 bytes, and inputs above 64 KiB are dropped. A current Desktop task hot reload is not established.
Scheduled page forget sweeps are disabled; upstream hollow-project cleanup remains enabled. Existing and unrelated account/model/scope settings remain unchanged.
Exact ai-memory lifetime/session saved tokens are not returned by upstream and remain null. Client consumption and upstream context estimates are separate.

Research workers stopped at account limits. Native Claude review first exceeded its turn limit; an incorrectly formed resume invocation failed; the retained resumed completion then supplied source-backed corrections.
Initial capture test filter selected zero tests and first Codex task lacked Stop because the modified hook was not yet trusted; corrected tests and real capture were qualified separately.
